title: Preparation and properties of intumescent flame retardant multilayer coatings treated ramie fabric/benzoxazine resin laminates
authors: Tao Zhang; Hongqiang Yan; Zhengping Fang
source_version: Published journal article in the official August 2016 issue; first online 13 October 2015
source_document_description: Official complete 268-page journal issue; this article occupies PDF pages 7–15, printed pages 1599–1607
source_material_form_TGA_raw: Ramie/BZ, MARamie/BZ and PARamie/BZ finished fabric/resin laminates in Table 2 and Figure 1; aliquot selection unreported
TGA_specimen_preparation: Approximately 8–10 mg of the prepared laminate was heated from room temperature to 600 °C in air at 20 °C/min. Cutting or grinding, through-thickness selection, assay-specific drying, gas flow, pan and replication are unreported.
LOI_method: GB/T 2406.2–2009; JF-3 oxygen index instrument, Chengde Dajia Instrument Co., Ltd.
LOI_statistic: Source tabulated scalar; averaging and replication unreported
LOI_specimen_preparation: Finished laminate specimens 120 × 6 × 3 mm; separate conditioning and number of replicates unreported.
source_numeric_evidence_description: Original Table 2 thermal data and Table 3 measured LOI, checked against the publisher PDF pages and own method. No numerical graph-coordinate extraction.
TG_locator: Printed pages 1600–1601, section 1.4, section 2.1, Table 2 and Figure 1; official issue PDF pages 8–9
LOI_locator: Printed page 1600, section 1.4; printed page 1602, Table 3 and section 2.2; official issue PDF pages 8 and 10
conditions_locator: Printed pages 1599–1600, sections 1.1–1.4 and Table 1; official issue PDF pages 7–8
source_location: Official issue PDF pages 7–15, printed article pages 1599–1607; Table 1 on page 1600, Table 2 on page 1601, Table 3 on page 1602
washing_state: Initial manufactured and cured laminate; no durability wash or ageing state assigned
treatment_method: Plain-woven ramie fabric from Jiangxi Jingzhu and PX-PN 001 benzoxazine monomer from Shanghai Chaoyu were used. Benzoxazine was diluted to 40 wt% in DMF at room temperature and methyl p-toluenesulfonate (PTSM) was added at 5 wt% relative to benzoxazine. The pristine or multilayer-coated fabric was immersed in that solution for 3 min at room temperature, then heated in a vacuum oven at 80 °C for 30 min. The prepregs were stacked and preheated at 120 °C for 15 min in a flat vulcanizing press. They were heated to 140 °C and held for 30 min at 5–6 MPa, then held at 160 °C for 30 min and 170 °C for 30 min, and naturally cooled to room temperature under pressure. The article does not state the ply count. Final component mass percentages are reported separately in Table 1.
source_T5_definition: Table 2 footnote explicitly defines T5% as 5 wt% mass-loss temperature.
source_Tmax_definition: Table 2 footnote calls Tmax1 and Tmax2 maximum mass-loss temperatures of the first and second steps; section 2.1 and Figure 1(b) identify the corresponding peaks of the derivative mass-loss curve, whose axis is differential residual mass in %/min. The second step is char oxidation.
source_residue_definition: Table 2 char residue from air TG at 600 °C, relative to the whole laminate specimen. Table 3 char residue is from the separate MCC experiment and is not used.
source_MCC_n_not_transferred: MCC uses three specimens of 3–5 mg under its own O2/N2 flow and 1 °C/s ramp; these conditions and repetitions do not describe TG or LOI.
limitations: The same three finished laminate labels occur in the composition table, air TG table and measured LOI table. Laminate components have different final mass fractions across treatments, which are retained as reported and are not renormalized to equal fabric content. The source specifies 20 multilayer deposition cycles and refers to earlier fabric-coating papers for detailed deposition and rinsing procedures; unreported dwell times, rinsing counts, pretreatment and add-on are not reconstructed. Table 1 reports coating content in the final laminate, not fabric add-on. TG pan, air flow, replicate count, drying and aliquot selection are unreported. LOI conditioning, averaging basis, uncertainty and replicate count are unreported. Three replicates and the oxygen/nitrogen flow in the nearby method belong to MCC only. The flame-test specimens are 3 mm thick, while mechanical-test specimens are 4 mm thick; TG does not identify the plate thickness or through-thickness selection. Table 1 presents one composition for each source label and does not identify separate ply populations. Table 2 supplies the TG values; no estimates are taken from Figure 1. The Table 3 residue and heat-release peak temperatures belong to MCC and are excluded. Earlier work on coated ramie fabrics is a precursor-form study, not this finished laminate. Related ramie/benzoxazine papers require a future control-level reuse comparison before their unfilled control is imported; numerical equivalence is unresolved. The Table 2 residue of 4 wt% at 600 °C is withheld because the corresponding Figure 1 terminal trace visibly falls below that tabulated value. The table value is preserved source-native; no graph-derived replacement is used.
composition: Table 1 final laminate mass fractions: ramie 65.50 wt%, benzoxazine 34.50 wt%, MWCNT-APP 0 wt%, PEI-APP 0 wt%
treatment_chemistry: No flame-retardant multilayer coating on the ramie fabric
pairing_evidence: Own Table 1 identifies Ramie/BZ as one final laminate formulation; its exact air TG row in Table 2 and measured LOI row in Table 3 carry this same source label and initial cured state. No fabric-precursor TG or MCC result is substituted.
source_title: Preparation and properties of intumescent flame retardant multilayer coatings treated ramie fabric/benzoxazine resin laminates
